meta.description: Faith FM's 'wh' command suite for Laravel Forge / LEMP web-hosting servers: a bash dispatcher that auto-detects site + project context from the filesystem and nginx config, then routes to per-command bash/python scripts covering code deployment, Docker, backups, WordPress database refresh, New Relic deployment markers, and server maintenance.
meta.generated_by: Claude Code static audit (read from source — no egress)

nodes.label: wh.sh
nodes.desc: The dispatcher. Derives every WH_* variable child scripts rely on — WH_USER/WH_SITE from the CWD path, WH_SITE_VALID + WH_WEBROOT_DIR + WH_PHP_CMD from /etc/nginx/sites-available/$WH_SITE (falling back to an included forge-conf/*/site.conf), and WH_PROJECT_DIR/WH_APP_NAME/WH_LARAVEL_DETECTED/WH_VITE_DETECTED/WH_VUE2|3_EXTRA_BUILD by walking upwards for a .git folder. Then execs wh-scripts/wh-<cmd>.sh (bash, with nvm pre-loaded) or wh-scripts/wh-<cmd>.py (python, under the repo venv).

nodes.label: wh.bash_completion
nodes.desc: Bash completion for `wh`: lists wh-scripts/wh-* and strips the 'wh-' prefix and extension to build the command word list. Installed to /etc/bash_completion.d/wh.

nodes.label: wh.crond
nodes.desc: System crontab fragment installed to /etc/cron.d/wh. Runs `wh nr-deployment-forward` as the forge user every minute, with MAILTO empty.

nodes.label: wh.pyenv-profile.d
nodes.desc: Installed to /etc/profile.d/pyenv.sh. Points PYENV_ROOT at the shared /home/shared/.pyenv, adds it to PATH, and runs `pyenv init -` so every login shell resolves the shared Python.

nodes.label: wh-checkout-github
nodes.desc: Forge deploy-script entrypoint. Fetches and hard-resets to origin/<branch> (default master) via `wh git`, so force-pushes deploy cleanly. Relies on the deploy script having cd'd into the site folder first.

nodes.label: wh-checkout-PR
nodes.desc: git post-receive hook entrypoint. Reads oldrev/newrev/ref lines from STDIN and checks out each newrev with `wh git checkout -f` + `git clean -f -d`. With --MASTER-BRANCH-ONLY it skips refs that don't end in /master — the guard used on production WordPress sites.

nodes.label: wh-composer-deploy
nodes.desc: The main post-checkout PHP deploy. cd's to WH_PROJECT_DIR, runs `wh composer install --no-interaction --prefer-dist --optimize-autoloader`, then for Laravel runs artisan queue:restart + cache:clear. If .gitignore mentions public/build it installs nvm-if-missing, `nvm install/use`, `npm ci` and runs whichever of `prod`/`build` npm scripts exist; repeats the npm build inside vue2/ and vue3/ when those folders were detected. Finishes with `wh fpm-reload` and `wh nr-deployment-capture`.

nodes.label: wh-composer-deploy-sessions
nodes.desc: Production-Laravel variant: deletes every file under $WH_PROJECT_DIR/storage/framework/sessions/ (forcing all users to re-login) and then delegates to wh-composer-deploy.

nodes.label: wh-docker-deploy
nodes.desc: Deploys the current project's container: calls `wh docker-copy-config` to materialise Dockerfile + docker-compose.yml from the shared templates, then `docker compose up --build --detach`.

nodes.label: wh-docker-down
nodes.desc: Stops the current project's container stack (`docker compose down`).

nodes.label: wh-docker-summary
nodes.desc: Server-wide report: scans /home/forge/dockerprojects/*/.env, parses each with the same quoting/comment rules bash `source` would apply, pairs each project folder with the proxy_pass port found in its nginx site file, and prints a tabulate grid sorted by DOCKER_PORT. Unreadable nginx configs and missing ports render as '-'.

nodes.label: wh-bup
nodes.desc: Bare `resticprofile` invocation — shows the snapshot list for the configured profile.

nodes.label: wh-bup-backup
nodes.desc: Manual backup run: `sudo -E resticprofile -v backup`, then chowns ~/.cache/restic back to $USER so the root-run backup doesn't leave an unusable cache.

nodes.label: wh-bup-config
nodes.desc: Creates ~/.config/resticprofile if needed, opens profiles.yaml in nano, then re-runs `wh bup-reschedule` so edited schedule times take effect.

nodes.label: wh-bup-reschedule
nodes.desc: `sudo -E resticprofile unschedule` followed by `schedule` — rebuilds the systemd timers from the current profiles.yaml.

nodes.label: wh-bup-unlock
nodes.desc: Clears a stale restic repository lock (`resticprofile unlock`).

nodes.label: wh-update
nodes.desc: The installer/updater. Checks WH_BASE_DIR is writable, hard-resets the repo to origin/master, then symlinks wh.sh → /usr/local/bin/wh and wh.bash_completion → /etc/bash_completion.d/wh, copies wh.crond → /etc/cron.d/wh (root:root 644) and wh.pyenv-profile.d → /etc/profile.d/pyenv.sh, pip-installs requirements.txt into venv/ if it exists, tightens repo permissions (o=x on the base dir, o=rx on wh-scripts), and ensures /var/log/app-deploys exists as forge:forge mode 1777 with an errors/ subfolder.

nodes.label: wh-python-update
nodes.desc: Occasional Python maintenance: apt-installs the pyenv build dependencies, clones or `git pull`s pyenv into $PYENV_DIR and rebuilds src/, installs the latest patch of $PYENV_VERSION, aborts with a 'restart your shell' warning if python3 doesn't yet match, then deletes and recreates venv/ and pip-installs requirements.txt.

nodes.label: wh-update-nvm
nodes.desc: Installs or updates nvm (resolving the latest tag from the GitHub API, then piping install.sh to bash) and sets the default node to the latest LTS. `--if-missing` makes it a no-op when ~/.nvm already exists — how wh-composer-deploy calls it.

nodes.label: wh-git-config
nodes.desc: One-off per-account git setup. Prints the exact commands, asks for y/n confirmation, then sets global user.email ($USER@$HOSTNAME), user.name, and advice.detachedHead=false — the identity that server-side checkouts and commits use.

nodes.label: wh-docker-install
nodes.desc: Installs Docker Engine per the official Ubuntu instructions (keyring, apt source, docker-ce + compose plugins) after a y/n prompt, then adds forge to the docker group and prints service status.

nodes.label: wh-bup-install
nodes.desc: Installs restic + resticprofile: maps `uname -m` to a Go arch, resolves each project's latest release by following the GitHub /releases/latest redirect, downloads and unpacks both binaries into /usr/local/bin as root:root 755, and writes /etc/sudoers.d/resticprofile granting forge NOPASSWD:SETENV for resticprofile.

nodes.label: wh-bup-selfupdate
nodes.desc: Runs the built-in `restic self-update` and `resticprofile self-update` under sudo.

nodes.label: wh-php
nodes.desc: Runs PHP as the *site's* version. Execs $WH_PHP_CMD (detected from nginx fastcgi_pass) when it exists on PATH; otherwise warns to stderr and falls back to the default `php`. Exists because a bare `php` on a multi-PHP server silently picks the default CLI version.

nodes.label: wh-composer
nodes.desc: Runs composer under the site's PHP version: resolves the composer binary with `command -v`, then execs `$WH_PHP_CMD <composer_bin> "$@"`. This is what keeps vendor/ — and any post-autoload-dump artisan hooks — matched to the runtime the site actually serves. Errors if composer is absent; warns and falls back if WH_PHP_CMD is unset or missing.

nodes.label: wh-git
nodes.desc: Git wrapper that resolves --git-dir/--work-tree for the current location. First tries wh-git-repos.yml in the enclosing /home/<user> folder, matching the CWD against each entry's bare or work path with a directory-boundary-safe comparison (so my-plugin-v2 doesn't match my-plugin). Otherwise, if CWD is the home folder itself it switches to the first domain-looking subfolder, then walks upwards for a .git directory. Exits 1 with an explanatory error when nothing resolves; otherwise runs git and propagates its return code.

nodes.label: wh-fpm-reload
nodes.desc: Reloads $WH_PHP_CMD-fpm. Uses `mkdir /tmp/fpmlockdir` as a mutex so concurrent deploys don't stack reloads — if the mkdir fails it prints 'Failed to acquire lock' and exits 1 rather than waiting.

nodes.label: wh-docker-get-context
nodes.desc: Sourced (not executed) by the other docker scripts. Sources $WH_PROJECT_ENV, then validates DOCKERFILE_TEMPLATE / DOCKERCOMPOSE_TEMPLATE and expands them into DOCKERFILE_TEMPLATE_PATH / DOCKERCOMPOSE_TEMPLATE_PATH under $WH_BASE_DIR/docker, exiting 1 with a specific message for each missing piece.

nodes.label: wh-docker-copy-config
nodes.desc: Sources wh-docker-get-context.sh then copies the two resolved templates into the project as Dockerfile and docker-compose.yml — i.e. project container config is regenerated from the shared templates on every deploy.

nodes.label: wh-nr-deployment-capture
nodes.desc: Captures the deployed commit. Strips git's local env vars (via `git rev-parse --local-env-vars`) so it works inside a post-receive hook, reads hash/author/date/message/timestamp from WH_PROJECT_DIR, optionally reads remote.origin.url, detects vendor/faithfm/new-relic-helper, and writes /var/log/app-deploys/<epoch>-<user>.log as JSON chmod 644.

nodes.label: wh-nr-deployment-forward
nodes.desc: Cron forwarder (runs every minute as forge). Loads NR_API_KEY from /home/forge/.env.wh-nr, then for each /var/log/app-deploys/*.log: parses it, looks up the New Relic entity GUID for 'PHP-H <app>' or 'PHP-N <app>' depending on nr_helper_detected, and posts a changeTrackingCreateDeployment GraphQL mutation with a GitHub commit deepLink. Successful files are deleted; failures are retried until 60s (parse errors) or 7 days (API errors) old, after which they move to errors/ with a syslog message.

nodes.label: wh-show-env
nodes.desc: Prints every WH_* variable the dispatcher computed — the first thing to run when a script misbehaves on a given site (e.g. to see whether WH_PHP_CMD or WH_PROJECT_DIR was detected).

nodes.label: wh-hello
nodes.desc: Minimal bash command — the template for adding a new `wh xyz` bash script.

nodes.label: wh-hello-python
nodes.desc: Minimal python command — also confirms which interpreter the venv actually resolves to.

nodes.label: .python-version
nodes.desc: Pins PYENV_VERSION for the whole suite; read by wh.sh on every invocation and by wh-python-update when installing Python.

nodes.label: requirements.txt
nodes.desc: Python deps for the venv the .py commands run under: PyYAML (wh-git), requests + python-dotenv (nr-deployment-forward), tabulate (docker-summary).

nodes.label: docker/.env.sample
nodes.desc: Reference .env for a containerised project: APP_* metadata, DOCKER_PORT, and the DOCKERFILE_TEMPLATE / DOCKERCOMPOSE_TEMPLATE names that select which shared templates get copied in.

nodes.label: template express01 Dockerfile
nodes.desc: Node 18.16.1 bookworm-slim image: npm ci --only=production, EXPOSE ${DOCKER_PORT}, `node server.js`. Selected by DOCKERFILE_TEMPLATE=express01.

nodes.label: template express01 docker-compose.yml
nodes.desc: Single `app` service built from the copied Dockerfile, restart:always, publishing ${DOCKER_PORT}:${DOCKER_PORT} under image ${APP_IMAGE_NAME}. Selected by DOCKERCOMPOSE_TEMPLATE=express01.

nodes.label: nginx site configs
nodes.desc: /etc/nginx/sites-available/<site> (plus included forge-conf/*/site.conf). The source of truth the suite reads for site validity, webroot, the site's PHP version (fastcgi_pass) and, for docker projects, the proxy_pass port.

nodes.label: PHP runtimes (multi-version)
nodes.desc: The several PHP versions installed per server — php8.x CLI binaries and php8.x-fpm services. The default CLI version is frequently older than the version a given site runs, which is the whole reason wh php / wh composer exist.

nodes.label: Forge deploy scripts & post-receive hooks
nodes.desc: The two triggers for all deployments: Laravel Forge deploy scripts fired by GitHub webhooks (production Laravel + Docker), and server-side git post-receive hooks (staging, and all WordPress plugins/themes). Both are two- or three-line scripts calling wh commands.

nodes.label: GitHub
nodes.desc: Origin remote for project checkouts and for this repo's own self-update; also the release API used by wh-update-nvm and wh-bup-install, and the base for New Relic deployment deepLinks.

nodes.label: wh-git-repos.yml
nodes.desc: Per-user file in /home/<user>/ pairing each bare repo with its working tree — how WordPress plugin/theme repos under git/plugins/ and git/themes/ get checked out into htdocs/wp-content/. A bare repo missing from this file will not deploy correctly.

nodes.label: project .env (WH_PROJECT_ENV)
nodes.desc: The deployed project's own .env. wh.sh reads APP_NAME from it (used as the New Relic app name); docker projects also supply DOCKER_PORT and the two template selectors from it.

nodes.label: /var/log/app-deploys
nodes.desc: The spool between capture and forward. forge:forge mode 1777 with the sticky bit, so every site user can drop a log file but cannot delete another user's; an errors/ subfolder holds quarantined files.

nodes.label: /home/forge/.env.wh-nr
nodes.desc: Holds NR_API_KEY for the New Relic forwarder. A manual post-install step — the forwarder exits 1 and syslogs if the file or key is missing.

nodes.label: New Relic GraphQL API
nodes.desc: api.newrelic.com/graphql — queried for the APM entity GUID by app name, then sent changeTrackingCreateDeployment mutations to place deployment markers.

nodes.label: shared pyenv + venv
nodes.desc: /home/shared/.pyenv plus the repo's venv/ folder. wh.sh activates the venv before running any .py command; /etc/profile.d/pyenv.sh makes pyenv available to login shells.

nodes.label: nvm + Node
nodes.desc: ~/.nvm. wh.sh sources it and re-exports the nvm function into bash child scripts, so wh-composer-deploy can `nvm install/use` per the project's .nvmrc before running npm ci.

nodes.label: Docker Engine / Compose
nodes.desc: The docker daemon and compose plugin driving containerised (Express / Apollo GraphQL) sites, which nginx reverse-proxies to on each project's DOCKER_PORT.

nodes.label: restic / resticprofile
nodes.desc: The backup binaries in /usr/local/bin, ~/.config/resticprofile/profiles.yaml, the scheduled timers, and the remote restic repository they write to.

nodes.label: wh-db-refresh-export
nodes.desc: Exports the current site's WordPress database as a hand-off bundle for a sibling site on the same server under a different unix user (prod → staging). Run as the source site's own user. Pre-flights options/setfacl/free space (needs ~2x the DB size in /tmp), dumps every prefixed table except --exclude via wp-cli mysqldump (--single-transaction so the live source is never locked, --set-gtid-purged=OFF to avoid needing SUPER on import), refuses to hand off a dump lacking the '-- Dump completed' tail, writes a manifest (table list, key row counts, source URL, core/db version, true dump byte size, views), then tars both into /tmp mode 600 under umask 077 with exactly one setfacl reader (--grant-user) — verified with getfacl before it is promised. Schedules its own deletion after --ttl minutes (default 120) via a detached sleeper whose liveness is checked. Any failure path removes everything via an EXIT trap.

nodes.label: wh-db-refresh-import
nodes.desc: Imports a hand-off bundle into the current site, re-points URLs, and runs acceptance checks — replacing third-party DB-sync plugins. Run as the target site's own user; all site-specific behaviour comes from an unversioned '.wh-db-refresh' beside the site, never from defaults. Gates first (manifest source_url matches config, hand-off age, prefix match, EXPECT_EXCLUDED really absent, target core >= source, free space). Then WordPress maintenance mode (a .maintenance 503 before plugins/cron, re-stamped every 4 min by a keepalive so long imports stay covered and hard-killed runs self-recover), import, cache reset, truncates, optional cron clear, core update-db. URLs are re-pointed serialized-safe via one host pass plus a scheme pass. Acceptance prints PASS/FAIL/WARN/INFO and exits 1 on any FAIL; maintenance is lifted ONLY if every *safety* check passed (import complete, truncates done, host rewritten, canary armed) — otherwise the site stays down with a far-future stamp and the recovery command is printed. Options are read straight from MySQL throughout, never get_option(), so a persistent object cache cannot turn the checks into vacuous passes.

nodes.label: db-refresh/.wh-db-refresh.sample
nodes.desc: Reference config copied to '<site>/.wh-db-refresh' on the importing side: SOURCE_URL, TRUNCATE_TABLES, EXPECT_EXCLUDED, CANARY_OPTION (clone-guard), ROW_DRIFT_PCT, MAX_HANDOFF_AGE_HOURS, CLEAR_CRON, SKIP_CACHE_FLUSH.

nodes.label: <site>/.wh-db-refresh
nodes.desc: Per-target-site import config, unversioned and living beside the site (like wh-git-repos.yml). Supplies every gate the import enforces; the import refuses to run without it. Table/option names are charset-validated before reaching SQL.

nodes.label: /tmp db-refresh hand-off
nodes.desc: The tar.gz bridging the two sites: manifest first (so the import can read it without unpacking the dump), then the SQL dump. Mode 600 plus a single setfacl read grant for the importing user; self-destructs on the exporter's TTL. Only its owner can delete it under sticky /tmp, which is why the export side self-cleans.

nodes.label: wp-cli + WordPress site/DB
nodes.desc: The 'wp' binary, the site's WordPress install under WH_WEBROOT_DIR, and its MySQL database. Both db-refresh commands invoke it as '$WH_PHP_CMD $(command -v wp) --path=<webroot>' so it runs under the site's PHP, and read options via raw SQL rather than get_option().
